verdict.headline: BUY / ADD — MOMENTUM IS EARNED, BUT IT IS BEING BOUGHT WITH DEBT
verdict.subhead: FUNDAMENTALS STRONG (margins expanding, guidance raised twice)   |   TECHNICALS BULLISH & CONSOLIDATING
verdict.summary: WMB scores 2.5/3.0. Growth and Peer are unambiguous 1.0s: management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $200M to $8.3-8.5B AND lifted the long-term target to 11%+ CAGR through 2030, on secular LNG and data-center demand that is contracted rather than cyclical, from the operator of Transco — the largest interstate gas pipeline in the United States. Quality is held at 0.5 for one reason: trailing free cash flow is NEGATIVE $174M, down from +$3,371M in FY2023, because capex has run to $6.17B with $7.3-7.9B guided for 2026. Margins are genuinely expanding (operating 31.4% to 38.1%, net 20.7% to 24.9% over two years) but the growth is being funded with debt and equity, not cash generation. Technicals are aligned and unstretched: price above both the 50- and 200-day, RSI in the neutral 46-54 band, 6.5% below the 52-week high, with a $85.47 consensus target 12.7% above the price.

assessment.heading: ASSESSMENT: ALIGNMENT, NOT DIVERGENCE — the risk here is the balance sheet, not the chart.
assessment.text: This is the rarer, less dramatic setup: fundamentals and technicals point the same way, so there is no divergence to arbitrage. The framework's job is then to find what the alignment hides — and it is the funding gap. Williams is converting an 11%+ growth target into $7-8B of annual capex while paying out 84% of earnings, which turns free cash flow negative and pushes leverage to 3.9x against a 4.0x internal ceiling. The margin expansion is real and the demand is contracted; the question is not whether the projects earn, but what the equity costs while they are built. That is a 0.5 on Quality, not a 1.0 — and it is why this is a 2.5 rather than the 3.0 the light triage assigned.

catalyst.title: Data-Center Power & LNG — Is Williams the Right Horse?

blocks.heading: 1. LNG exports double within the decade
bullets: Management expects US LNG exports to roughly double, with Haynesville production growing 10+ Bcf/d to feed it. Williams' Louisiana Energy Gateway and the new Momentum assets sit directly on that path from wellhead to Gulf Coast liquefaction.

blocks.heading: 2. Transco is the data-center toll road
bullets: Transco Power Express was upsized to an 800 Mcf/d expansion serving Virginia data centers and power demand. Southeast Supply Enhancement and Power Express are both described by management as purely organic — no acquisition required to capture them.

blocks.heading: 3. Behind-the-meter, already in service
bullets: Socrates Phase 1 reached 200 MW in service in under 18 months, and management reports discussions with multiple customers beyond the initial hyperscaler. Blackstone committed $5.34B to the Power Innovation JV, including $4.4B for 49% of growth capex at a capped 6.35% cost of equity.

blocks.heading: 1. The growth is volume-led, not rate-led
bullets: Management characterised growth as coming primarily through new infrastructure connections rather than rate increases. The framework's heuristic scores price/mix-led growth above volume-led — mitigated here because the volume is take-or-pay contracted against new structural demand, not a cyclical restock.

blocks.heading: 2. Free cash flow has gone negative
bullets: TTM FCF is -$174M against +$3,371M in FY2023. Operating cash flow is healthy at $5.99B; the gap is $6.17B of capex, guided to $7.3-7.9B in 2026. Every dollar of the 11%+ CAGR is being pre-funded.

blocks.heading: 3. Paid for with debt and equity
bullets: The $5.5B Momentum acquisition was $3.5B cash/debt plus $2B equity at ~8.5x projected 2027 EBITDA. Year-end leverage is guided to 3.9x against a 4.0x internal ceiling, leaving just over $2B of headroom.

verdict.text: TREND VERDICT: RIGHT HORSE, FULL PRICE — Williams is a pure-play on gas-fired power and LNG feedgas, not a peripheral beneficiary, and Blackstone underwriting 49% of growth capex at a capped 6.35% is third-party validation of that position. Unlike a narrative trade, the exposure is contracted and already partly in service. The discipline is on entry price and size, not on whether the thesis is real.

parts.title: Part 1 — Quality Check (Margins & Profitability)
parts.question: Is the price move supported by margin trends?

rows.t: CLEARLY EXPANDING — operating margin 31.41% (FY24) to 37.45% (FY25) to 38.14% (TTM); net margin 20.66% to 22.11% to 24.91%. Roughly 670bps of operating margin in two years.
IMPROVING off a healthy base — ROE 15.78% (FY24) to 18.55% (FY25) to 21.50%; ROIC 6.53% to 7.84% to 7.95%.
NEGATIVE — -$174M TTM, against +$899M (FY25), +$2,296M (FY24) and +$3,371M (FY23). Operating cash flow is healthy at $5,994M; capex of $6,168M is the entire gap.
STRETCHING — total debt $30.79B, debt/equity 2.00, payout ratio 83.67%, leverage guided to 3.9x against a 4.0x internal ceiling.

rows: Structural, not cost-cutting: Transmission & Gulf expansion projects entering service plus higher natural gas storage revenues — contracted capacity, which is why the gain has held for two consecutive years.

rows.t: The margin series is genuinely expanding off a healthy base — this is not the LNG case where no reported series was moving. But the rubric's 1.0 requires strong FCF alongside expanding margins, and FCF is negative. Growth is being pre-funded with debt and equity while 84% of earnings goes out as dividends.

finalVerdict.reasoning: Fundamentals score 2.5/3 and technicals are bullish without being stretched, which the rubric maps directly to BUY / ADD. There is no divergence to exploit here — the two sides agree — so the discipline moves from timing to sizing. The single reservation is Quality: free cash flow has swung from +$3.37B (FY23) to -$174M on a capex programme guided at $7.3-7.9B for 2026, with leverage heading to 3.9x against a 4.0x ceiling and 84% of earnings paid out. That is a deliberate, contracted, well-underwritten build — Blackstone is funding 49% of growth capex at a capped 6.35% — but it means the equity carries construction risk until those projects earn. Buy it toward the 200-day rather than at the range top, keep the stop at $69.50, and note that the lowest Street target ($69) sits exactly there: if the low case is right, the stop is the trade.
